_note: The stock starter car's Step 6 results at full precision (every test but the timing one): the stock car must keep giving exactly these. Re-recorded in Phase 2 Step 8 (the test driver learnt to lift off as the rear slides or the driven wheels spin), and again in Fixes and engine upgrades: (1) the auto-clutch no longer slips after a shift while the car's moving (it used to slip the 1st→2nd change like a CVT, holding the engine near its launch revs) and the stock gearbox changes gear in 0.2 s rather than 0.25, so clutch out, gear and clutch in take about 0.3 s: without the slipping clutch keeping the engine near peak power, 0–100 is 0.1 s slower (9.22 s), the quarter mile 0.07 s (16.82 s) and the lap 0.18 s (77.69 s); braking moves in the last digits (it drives up to speed first); (2) a car put down already moving (the skidpad and slalom start that way) now starts with its wheels turning and no parking hold (they used to start locked): skidpad 0.83716 g, slalom 8.70 s.
